title_en: Jiangsu Nantong Liujian Construction Group Co., Ltd. v. Hengshui Hongtai Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over a construction project contract
ruling_gist_en: Article 205 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides that a party applying for retrial shall file the application within six months after the judgment or ruling becomes legally effective; if the circumstances specified in Items 1, 3, 12, and 13 of Article 200 of this Law exist, the application shall be filed within six months from the date the party knows or should have known of such circumstances. This Article provides for the time limit for a party to apply for retrial. The reason why the law provides for a time limit for applying for retrial is, on the one hand, to maintain the res judicata of effective judgments, to prevent the legal rights and obligations determined by effective judgments from remaining in an unstable state subject to possible retrial for a long time, thereby maintaining the stability of social relations; on the other hand, to urge the parties to exercise their right to apply for retrial in a timely manner, and to avoid affecting the reliance interests of the opposing party on the stability of the effective judgment. Accordingly, if a party applies for retrial on grounds other than those specified in Items 1, 3, 12, and 13 of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law, the application shall be filed within six months after the judgment or ruling becomes legally effective; if a party, after six months from the effective date of the judgment or ruling, files an application for retrial on the grounds specified in Items 1, 3, 12, and 13 of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law and simultaneously raises other grounds for retrial, the people's court shall not examine such other grounds.

full_text_en:
Jiangsu Nantong Liujian Construction Group Co., Ltd. v. Hengshui Hongtai Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over construction project contract

Ruling Summary

Article 205 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC provides that a party applying for retrial shall file the application within six months after the judgment or ruling becomes legally effective; where the circumstances provided in Items 1, 3, 12, and 13 of Article 200 of this Law exist, the application shall be filed within six months from the date the party knows or should have known of such circumstances. This article sets forth the time limit for a party to apply for retrial. The reason why the law stipulates a time limit for applying for retrial is, on the one hand, to maintain the res judicata effect of an effective judgment and to avoid the legal rights and obligations determined by the effective judgment from being in a state of uncertainty susceptible to retrial for a long period, thereby maintaining the stability of social relations; on the other hand, it is to urge the party to exercise the right to apply for retrial in a timely manner, so as to avoid affecting the other party's reliance interest in the stability of the effective judgment. Accordingly, if a party applies for retrial on grounds other than those specified in Items 1, 3, 12, and 13 of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law, the application shall be filed within six months after the judgment or ruling becomes legally effective; if, after six months from the effective date of the judgment or ruling, the party applies for retrial on the grounds specified in Items 1, 3, 12, and 13 of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law and at the same time raises other grounds for retrial, the people's court shall not examine such other grounds.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court
(2018) Zui Gao Fa Min Shen No. 6278

Retrial Applicant (Plaintiff at First Instance, Counterclaim Defendant, Appellant at Second Instance): Jiangsu Nantong Liujian Construction Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at Fushou Road, Rucheng Town, Rugao City, Jiangsu Province.
Legal Representative: Shen Weidong, General Manager of the company.
Authorized Litigation Agents: Li Qiang, lawyer of Hebei Shiji Lianhe Law Firm.
Authorized Litigation Agents: Liu Miao, lawyer of Hebei Shiji Lianhe Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Counterclaim Plaintiff, Appellant at Second Instance): Hengshui Hongtai Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at Yongxing Road, Taocheng District, Hengshui City, Hebei Province.
Legal Representative: Bai Yunxiang, Manager of the company.

The retrial applicant, Jiangsu Nantong Liujian Construction Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Nantong Liujian), applied to this Court for retrial of the civil judgment (2013) Ji Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 330 rendered by the Hebei High People's Court in the case of dispute over a construction project contract with the respondent, Hengshui Hongtai Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hongtai Company). This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to examine this case, and the examination has now been concluded.

Nantong Liujian applied for retrial on the following grounds: First, new evidence, the "Notice of Unqualified Fire Protection Design Record Review for Construction Project" issued by the Hengshui Municipal Public Security Fire Brigade on September 5, 2018, states that the fire protection design documents for the CBD East 6# and 8# residential building projects submitted by Hongtai Company indicated that part of the fire protection design of the project did not comply with the relevant fire protection technical standards and was unqualified. Therefore, the project itself had passed completion acceptance, and the fundamental reason for failing the comprehensive acceptance was the unqualified fire protection design of Hongtai Company, not the responsibility of Nantong Liujian. Second, the second instance judgment, which required Nantong Liujian to first deliver the project acceptance data to Hongtai Company and made this a prerequisite for Hongtai Company to pay the project price, did not comply with the contract and was a misapprehension of facts. Third, the second instance judgment's determination that Hongtai Company should pay Nantong Liujian project price of RMB 4,174,750 was erroneous; the actual amount of project price owed by Hongtai Company was RMB 12,793,785. Fourth, the second instance judgment's failure to support Nantong Liujian's claim for a 7% reduction on the original amount of the deduction items was a violation of the contract. Fifth, the second instance judgment's determination that Nantong Liujian had waived its claim for "liquidated damages and other losses" was a misapprehension of facts. Sixth, deducting RMB 149,000 for coordination fees and RMB 530,400 for heat meter replacement fees from the payable project price in the second instance judgment had no factual or legal basis. In summary, Nantong Liujian applied for retrial pursuant to Item 1 of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC.

Upon examination, this Court finds that the court of first instance only tried and rendered a judgment on the project price, and the court of second instance also adjudicated on the amount of project price owed by Hongtai Company to Nantong Liujian. The specific amount of the project price between the parties has no bearing on whether the fire protection design was qualified or whether the project passed comprehensive acceptance. Moreover, delivering the completion acceptance report and corresponding completion data is a contractual obligation that Nantong Liujian, as the contractor, must perform, and it is also unrelated to whether the fire protection design was qualified or whether the project passed comprehensive acceptance. Therefore, the new evidence submitted by Nantong Liujian, the "Notice of Unqualified Fire Protection Design Record Review for Construction Project," is insufficient to overturn the judgments of the courts of first and second instance regarding the amount of project price involved and the obligation to deliver the project acceptance data for the project in question, and does not constitute new evidence for retrial within the meaning of Item 1 of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC.

Article 205 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC provides that a party applying for retrial shall file the application within six months after the judgment or ruling becomes legally effective; where the circumstances provided in Items 1, 3, 12, and 13 of Article 200 of this Law exist, the application shall be filed within six months from the date the party knows or should have known of such circumstances. This article sets forth the time limit for a party to apply for retrial. The reason why the law stipulates a time limit for applying for retrial is, on the one hand, to maintain the res judicata effect of an effective judgment and to avoid the legal rights and obligations determined by the effective judgment from being in a state of uncertainty susceptible to retrial for a long period, thereby maintaining the stability of social relations; on the other hand, it is to urge the party to exercise the right to apply for retrial in a timely manner, so as to avoid affecting the other party's reliance interest in the stability of the effective judgment. Accordingly, if a party applies for retrial on grounds other than those specified in Items 1, 3, 12, and 13 of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law, the application shall be filed within six months after the judgment or ruling becomes legally effective; if, after six months from the effective date of the judgment or ruling, the party applies for retrial on the grounds specified in Items 1, 3, 12, and 13 of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law and at the same time raises other grounds for retrial, the people's court shall not examine such other grounds. Otherwise, it would indirectly encourage or condone a party who fails to comply with the time limit for applying for retrial to abuse the right to apply for retrial, rendering the six-month time limit for applying for retrial meaningless.

In this case, the second instance judgment was rendered on December 22, 2014. The other grounds for retrial raised by Nantong Liujian, apart from Item 1 of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law, should have been raised within six months after the second instance judgment became legally effective. Nantong Liujian applied for retrial on November 16, 2018, based on Item 1 of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law, while also raising other grounds for retrial. Since these other grounds were raised beyond the statutory six-month period for applying for retrial, this Court will not examine them.

In conclusion, the application for retrial by Nantong Liujian does not meet the circumstances provided in Item 1 of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC. Pursuant to paragraph 1 of Article 204 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC and paragraph 2 of Article 395 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the ruling is as follows:

The application for retrial by Jiangsu Nantong Liujian Construction Group Co., Ltd. is dismissed.

Presiding Judge: Fu Shaojun
Judge: Liu Yinchun
Judge: Si Wei
December 25, 2018
Court Clerk: Wu Zelong
